method: Differential whole-file review against fully read Unix SSE4.1 assembly: full321-line unified diff inspected without truncation; remaining lines verified text-identical with SequenceMatcher autojunk disabled. Not an independent serial reread of identical lines.
findings: Hash-many adds RSI/RDI preservation,528-byte reservation and saves XMM6..15 at aligned offsets0x170..0x200. Existing message/counter scratch remains below those saves. All saves are restored at common return.

Windows four register arguments are reshuffled to internal SysV-style register layout; stacked counter/increment/flags/start/end/output use RBP offsets0x68/70/78/80/88/90 after eight pushes. Tail flag reads adjusted too; jnz versus jne is equivalent.

Both scalar entry points subtract120 bytes, aligning entry stack for seven16-byte saves: XMM6,7,8,9,11,14,15. Registers XMM10/12/13 are not used in these scalar cores. Restore sequences and stack additions balance on inspected returns.

Scalar Windows CV/block pointers use RCX/RDX, length R8b, counter R9, flags at adjusted RSP+0xA0. Both explicitly zero-extend byte length and flags. XOF output pointer at RSP+0xA8 goes to volatile R10, and four16-byte stores produce64 output bytes.

Shared SIMD round arithmetic, batch4/2/1 decomposition and constants remain unchanged apart from address/register adaptations. Read-only section becomes .rdata; ELF CET/GNU-stack and Apple conditionals disappear.
No explicit Windows unwind metadata directives appear. Source adaptation is not proof of assembly, ABI correctness during exceptions, CPU dispatch or runtime parity.
limits: 281/289 pinned blobs reviewed; global complete repositories150/500.
No Windows/x86 execution, sanitizer or speed measurements. Upstream remains reference-only; pHash/ASAN deferred.
